16. "He had been blind to all the small slights, and omissions of trivial ceremonies" — present in draft.
17. The voice/irony of "I am sure he was startled" is gone — low issue.
18. Alderney cow — "the proposal, if ever it was made, was knocked on the head by Captain Brown's decided..." — draft changes to "when Captain Brown's decided counsel cut through all" — slight paraphrase, minor.
19. Party scene — "Parties in Cranford were solemn festivities, making the ladies feel gravely elated as they sat together in their best dresses." — draft has "Parties in Cranford were solemn festivities" but drops "making the ladies feel gravely elated as they sat together in their best dresses." This is a signature phrase.
20. "Miss Jenkyns sat in patient gravity" — ABSENT from draft. This is a distinctive, iconic sentence-moment in the Dickens vs. Johnson scene.
21. "and so on, till we blinded ourselves to the vulgar fact that we were, all of us, people of very moderate means" — absent from draft.
22. The Pickwick exchange — largely preserved verbatim, good.
23. "She thought she would give him a finishing blow or two" — draft has "She thought to give him a finishing blow" — "or two" dropped, minor.

Key findings:

1. **"Miss Jenkyns sat in patient gravity"** — absent. Iconic sentence in the famous literary debate scene. High-recognition phrase.
2. **"making the ladies feel gravely elated as they sat together in their best dresses"** — absent from draft's party-description sentence.
3. **"and so on, till we blinded ourselves to the vulgar fact that we were, all of us, people of very moderate means"** — absent; this is the rhetorical climax of the poverty-concealment passage.
4. **The smoking chimney / "walked upstairs, nothing daunted, spoke in a voice too large for the room"** — flattened.
